items: Rapid-onset red swollen tender joint, often overnight; fever possible
Chronic gout: tophi on ears/olecranon, erosive arthritis; recurrent flares separated by asymptomatic intervals
CPPD in younger adults → investigate associated metabolic disorders

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Crystal phagocytosis activates inflammasome/IL-1 → neutrophilic synovitis
Most hyperuricemia reflects reduced renal urate excretion rather than excessive production

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ First/atypical acute monoarthritis → **arthrocentesis**, polarized microscopy, Gram stain/culture
★ **Crystals do not exclude septic arthritis**; serum urate may be normal during gout flare
Chronic imaging: punched-out defects with overhanging edges; ultrasound double-contour sign supports urate deposition

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Acute crystal flare → **indomethacin/other NSAID, colchicine, or glucocorticoid**; joint steroid after excluding infection
NSAID failure → switch class; older exam questions may expect potent NSAID, e.g. indomethacin
CKD/ulcer/anticoagulation → favor steroid; adjust colchicine for renal impairment/interactions; avoid NSAIDs in advanced CKD
★ Urate lowering: **allopurinol first-line**, including CKD; start low, titrate to serum urate <6 mg/dL
Urate lowering doesn't treat flares; continue through flares; may start mid-flare (older exam questions: wait)

rows.label: Complications
items: Gout: destructive arthritis, uric-acid stones; CPPD: chronic degenerative/inflammatory arthropathy
Allopurinol hypersensitivity; colchicine → diarrhea/neuromyopathy
Xanthine-oxidase inhibitors + azathioprine/6-MP → severe marrow suppression

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Urate lowering: **tophi, joint damage, ≥2 flares/year**; first flare with CKD ≥3/stones/urate >9 → consider
Starting urate lowering → colchicine/NSAID prophylaxis 3–6 months; serial urate monitoring; not for isolated hyperuricemia
Uncomplicated first flare → **limit alcohol/fructose**, lose weight; thiazide → losartan; keep indicated aspirin
Before allopurinol: HLA-B*58:01 testing with Southeast Asian/African American ancestry; CPPD lacks crystal-depleting drugs

rows.label: Mimics
items: Septic arthritis: positive culture, bacteremia risk; aspiration essential when uncertain
Cellulitis: superficial inflammation, less restriction of passive joint motion
RA: persistent symmetric small-joint synovitis

gout.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [ACR gout guideline 2020](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10563586/), [ACR gout education 2025](https://rheumatology.org/patients/gout); CPPD established teaching.

hearing-loss.name: Hearing loss
hearing-loss.scope: Conductive vs sensorineural hearing loss, Weber and Rinne tests, presbycusis, ototoxicity (cisplatin, aminoglycosides, loop diuretics), noise-induced, Meniere disease, acoustic neuroma
hearing-loss.core: Distinguish impaired sound conduction from cochlear/nerve dysfunction; sudden sensorineural loss requires urgent treatment rather than observation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Aging, occupational/recreational noise, cerumen, chronic middle-ear disease
★ Ototoxins: **cisplatin, aminoglycosides, loop diuretics**; risk increases with renal impairment and combined exposure

rows.label: Clues
items: Presbycusis: bilateral high-frequency loss, difficulty understanding speech amid background noise
Noise injury: high-frequency audiometric notch; tinnitus common
Ménière: episodic vertigo, fluctuating low-frequency loss, tinnitus, aural fullness
★ **Unilateral progressive loss + poor speech discrimination** → vestibular schwannoma; imbalance may accompany

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Conductive: external/middle-ear transmission impaired; sensorineural: cochlea or auditory nerve damaged
Chronic noise/aging preferentially damages basal cochlear hair cells; Ménière involves endolymphatic hydrops

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Otoscopy → tuning forks → formal audiometry**, including air/bone thresholds and speech testing
Tympanometry evaluates middle-ear mechanics; asymmetric sensorineural loss → MRI internal auditory canals
Sudden loss: ≥30 dB across ≥3 contiguous frequencies within 72 hours; urgent audiogram/ENT
Do not attribute sudden unilateral deficit to cerumen without confirming resolution after removal

rows.label: Tx
items: Remove cerumen, treat effusion/infection or structural cause; persistent conductive disease → ENT
★ Sudden sensorineural loss → **corticosteroids promptly**, within 2 weeks; intratympanic route possible
Chronic bilateral deficit → hearing aids, communication strategies; severe refractory loss → cochlear implant evaluation
Ménière: sodium moderation, selected diuretic; short-term vestibular suppressant during attacks
Vestibular schwannoma: observation, stereotactic radiation, or surgery according to tumor size and symptoms

rows.label: Complications
items: Communication barriers, social isolation, depression, impaired safety awareness
Ototoxicity can be permanent; vestibular injury can cause imbalance and falls

rows.label: Prevention
items: Hearing protection, safe listening levels, baseline/serial audiometry with ototoxic drugs

rows.label: Mimics
items: Auditory processing/cognitive disorder: difficulty understanding despite relatively preserved peripheral thresholds
BPPV: brief positional vertigo without hearing loss

heart-failure.name: Heart failure
heart-failure.scope: HFrEF, HFpEF, acute decompensated heart failure, cardiogenic flash pulmonary edema, guideline-directed medical therapy, neurohormonal activation (RAAS, ADH-mediated hyponatremia)
heart-failure.core: Inadequate cardiac output or elevated filling pressures → pulmonary or systemic congestion, even with a normal ejection fraction.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: CAD, hypertension, valvular disease, cardiomyopathy, alcohol, cardiotoxic chemotherapy
Decompensation triggers: ischemia, infection, arrhythmia, missed diuretics, NSAIDs

rows.label: Clues
items: Orthopnea, paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, elevated JVP, crackles or wheeze (cardiac asthma), dependent edema
S3 suggests volume overload; S4 suggests stiff ventricle
★ **Flash edema**: abrupt respiratory distress, severe hypertension, pink frothy sputum

rows.label: Pathophys
items: RAAS/sympathetic activation → vasoconstriction, sodium retention, adverse remodeling
Low effective volume → baroreceptor-driven nonosmotic **ADH** release → dilutional hyponatremia; marker of advanced disease
Alveolar flooding → V/Q mismatch, widened A-a gradient, hypoxemia
High-output HF: severe anemia, AV fistula (larger fistula → more shunt); HF signs with **normal/high EF**

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Echocardiography**: EF, valves, wall motion; ECG, CXR, BNP support diagnosis
Low BNP argues against HF; obesity lowers BNP, renal dysfunction raises it
Identify precipitant: troponin, CBC, electrolytes, creatinine; evaluate ischemic cause

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Acute congestion → **IV furosemide**; hypoxemia → oxygen; respiratory distress → noninvasive ventilation
★ Hypertensive pulmonary edema → **IV nitroglycerin**; shock → norepinephrine ± dobutamine, urgent cause correction
Congested HFrEF → loop diuretic + **ACE inhibitor/ARNI first**; beta-blocker/MRA once compensated; ACE inhibitor → ARNI: 36-hour washout
MRA: eGFR >30, K <5; never ACE inhibitor + ARB; EF ≤35% despite GDMT → consider ICD
HFrEF foundation drugs lower mortality; loop diuretics, nitrates alone, digoxin relieve symptoms only

rows.label: Complications
items: Cardiorenal syndrome, ventricular arrhythmia, sudden death, hepatic congestion
Diuresis → hypokalemia; RAAS blockade → hyperkalemia, renal dysfunction; monitor creatinine/K

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Daily weights, sodium moderation, adherence; **continue GDMT after EF recovery**
Treat hypertension, CAD, AF; smoking cessation, exercise, influenza/pneumococcal vaccination

rows.label: Mimics
items: COPD: obstructive spirometry, hyperinflation
Nephrotic syndrome: heavy proteinuria, hypoalbuminemia
PE: pleuritic pain, thrombotic risk, RV strain
ARDS: diffuse infiltrates, no cephalization; massive crystalloid + **cephalization/perihilar fullness** → volume overload

table.title: Chronic phenotypes
rows: Sacubitril/valsartan (or ACEi/ARB), carvedilol/metoprolol succinate, spironolactone, dapagliflozin

heart-failure.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [ACC HFrEF 2024](https://www.acc.org/Latest-in-Cardiology/ten-points-to-remember/2024/03/06/19/22/2024-acc-expert-consensus-hfref); other points established teaching.

hematuria.name: Hematuria
hematuria.scope: Microscopic hematuria, gross hematuria, dipstick confirmation with urine sediment, glomerular vs extraglomerular workup, cystoscopy and CT urography indications
hematuria.core: Urinary RBCs require localization to glomerular versus urologic bleeding, then malignancy evaluation based on risk.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Urothelial cancer: older age, smoking, aromatic amines, pelvic radiation, cyclophosphamide

rows.label: Clues
items: Clots favor urologic bleeding; edema and hypertension suggest nephritis
★ Painless visible bleeding → malignancy concern even if transient
Colicky flank pain suggests stone; dysuria and urgency favor infection

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Glomerular capillary injury permits RBC passage; tubular transit distorts RBCs and forms casts

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Positive dipstick → **urine microscopy**; ≥3 RBC/hpf on properly collected specimen defines microhematuria
★ RBC casts, dysmorphic RBCs, proteinuria or renal dysfunction → nephrology plus risk-based urologic evaluation
★ Unexplained gross bleeding → **cystoscopy + CT urography**; MR urography if contrast CT contraindicated
Assess age, sex, smoking, RBC count and gross bleeding history; anticoagulation does not change evaluation

rows.label: Tx
items: UTI → antibiotics, then repeat microscopy after resolution; persistent RBCs → risk-stratified workup
Clot retention → large-bore three-way Foley, irrigation, urgent urology

rows.label: Complications
items: Obstructive AKI from clots; anemia with sustained bleeding

rows.label: Prevention
items: Smoking cessation to reduce future urothelial cancer risk

rows.label: Mimics
items: Myoglobinuria or hemoglobinuria: positive heme with absent RBCs
Food or phenazopyridine discoloration: red urine with negative heme

table.title: Microscopic hematuria workup by malignancy risk
rows: Same anatomic workup as gross bleeding

hemolytic-anemias.name: Hemolytic Anemias
hemolytic-anemias.scope: autoimmune hemolytic anemia (warm and cold agglutinins), hereditary spherocytosis, G6PD deficiency, DAT/Coombs testing, peripheral smear, complications
hemolytic-anemias.core: Reticulocytosis, elevated LDH/indirect bilirubin and reduced haptoglobin suggest hemolysis; DAT and smear identify the mechanism.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Autoimmune disease, CLL, drugs → immune hemolysis; infections can trigger cold-antibody disease
Family history → inherited membrane/enzyme defect; oxidants, fava beans or infection trigger G6PD crises
Coombs-negative newborn jaundice after maternal oxidant drug → consider G6PD; X-linked, Mediterranean ancestry

rows.label: Clues
items: Fatigue, pallor, jaundice, dark urine; splenomegaly suggests chronic extravascular destruction
Severe intravascular lysis → hemoglobinuria, back pain, AKI; hemoglobin decline can outpace reticulocyte response
Spherocytes occur in hereditary and warm immune disease; morphology alone cannot distinguish them
Childhood gallstones + splenomegaly + family history → hereditary spherocytosis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Extravascular: splenic/hepatic macrophage clearance; intravascular: RBC destruction within circulation
Free hemoglobin consumes haptoglobin; marrow compensates unless infection, deficiency or marrow failure limits production
Hereditary spherocytosis: ankyrin/spectrin cytoskeleton defect changes RBC shape → trapping in splenic red pulp

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **CBC, reticulocytes, LDH, bilirubin, haptoglobin**, peripheral smear
★ **DAT/Coombs** detects immune coating; negative test redirects toward nonimmune causes
Hereditary spherocytosis → eosin-5-maleimide binding test; usually normocytic, normochromic; ↑MCHC supports
G6PD activity can be falsely normal during crisis/after transfusion → repeat after recovery
Schistocytes → evaluate microangiopathy/mechanical destruction urgently, including platelet count and renal function

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Severe symptomatic anemia → **transfuse promptly** with blood-bank coordination; do not await perfect compatibility
Warm AIHA → glucocorticoids; refractory → rituximab or selected splenectomy
Cold disease → warmth, treat cause; rituximab-based treatment when symptomatic; steroids usually ineffective
G6PD → stop oxidant, treat trigger, supportive transfusion when severe
Hereditary spherocytosis → folate; selected severe disease → splenectomy after immunization

rows.label: Complications
items: Pigment gallstones, folate deficiency, aplastic crisis; chronic immune disease increases thrombosis risk
Splenectomy → encapsulated infection and thrombosis; intravascular disease → renal injury

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ G6PD: avoid **dapsone, primaquine, rasburicase, sulfonamides** and other oxidants
Before splenectomy: pneumococcal/meningococcal/Hib vaccines; infection education and selected antibiotic prophylaxis

rows.label: Mimics
items: Blood loss: reticulocytosis without hemolytic chemistry
Gilbert syndrome: isolated indirect bilirubin without anemia

table.title: Mechanism signatures
rows: Bite cells; Heinz bodies on supravital stain

hemolytic-anemias.evidence: Not checked online; established hematology teaching.

herpes-simplex-virus.name: Herpes simplex virus
herpes-simplex-virus.scope: HSV-1 and HSV-2, genital herpes, neonatal herpes, herpes labialis, eczema herpeticum, acyclovir
herpes-simplex-virus.core: Painful grouped vesicles recurring at mucocutaneous sites reflect latent HSV reactivation; neonatal infection and disseminated disease require urgent systemic treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Skin/mucosal contact, asymptomatic shedding, new sexual partners; either HSV type can cause genital disease
Immunosuppression, atopic dermatitis; neonatal risk highest with newly acquired maternal infection near delivery

rows.label: Clues
items: Primary genital: fever, tender nodes, dysuria, painful ulcers, 2–3 weeks; recurrences milder, resolve within 1 week
Labialis: tingling prodrome, vermilion cluster; **whitlow**: painful grouped finger vesicles after oral-secretion exposure
★ **Monomorphic punched-out erosions in eczema** → eczema herpeticum; ocular symptoms threaten vision
Neonate: sepsislike illness, vesicles sometimes absent; seizures/hepatitis suggest CNS or disseminated disease

rows.label: Pathophys
items: HSV establishes sensory ganglion latency; stress, illness, UV exposure trigger reactivation
Genital HSV-2 recurs/sheds more than genital HSV-1

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Active lesion → **HSV PCR/NAAT with typing**; culture less sensitive as lesions heal
Encephalitis/neonatal CNS concern, **lymphocytic CSF with RBCs** → CSF HSV PCR; early negative may require repeat
Neonate → lesion/surface, blood, CSF testing plus liver enzymes; treat while testing
No routine type-specific serology screening or HSV IgM

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ First genital episode → **oral acyclovir or valacyclovir for 7–10 days**; start before results
Recurrence → prompt episodic dosing at prodrome; frequent/distressing episodes → daily suppressive valacyclovir
★ Neonatal, CNS, disseminated disease or severe eczema herpeticum → **IV acyclovir**
Pregnancy: acyclovir/valacyclovir from 36 weeks; labor lesions/prodrome → cesarean; neither → vaginal despite history
Corneal involvement → urgent ophthalmology; avoid unsupervised ocular corticosteroids

rows.label: Complications
items: Encephalitis, aseptic meningitis, urinary retention, keratitis, dissemination; increased HIV acquisition risk
Acyclovir → crystal nephropathy, neurotoxicity with renal impairment; hydrate, adjust dose

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Avoid sex during lesions/prodrome**, condoms, partner disclosure; suppression lowers but never eliminates transmission
Avoid kissing infants with active labialis; cover lesions, hand hygiene

rows.label: Mimics
items: Syphilis: classically painless chancre; chancroid: deep purulent painful ulcer
Aphthae: mucosal ulcers, no preceding vesicles
Zoster: unilateral dermatomal eruption
Felon/paronychia: pus, no vesicles; whitlow → oral acyclovir, **no incision/drainage**

herpes-simplex-virus.evidence: Checked genital disease 2026-10-30: [CDC HSV guidance](https://www.cdc.gov/std/treatment-guidelines/herpes.htm); neonatal/eczema management established teaching.

table.title: Neonatal IV acyclovir duration
rows: ≥21 days; CNS: confirm CSF PCR clearance

herpes-zoster.name: Herpes zoster
herpes-zoster.scope: Varicella zoster reactivation, dermatomal rash, herpes zoster ophthalmicus, Ramsay Hunt syndrome, oral antivirals, postherpetic neuralgia, Shingrix vaccine
herpes-zoster.core: Latent varicella-zoster reactivation causes painful unilateral dermatomal vesicles; ophthalmic involvement or disseminated disease changes urgency and treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Older age, HIV, malignancy, transplantation, immunosuppressive drugs
Previous chickenpox or live varicella vaccination establishes latency; no new exposure required

rows.label: Clues
items: Burning/allodynia can precede eruption by days; crops crust over approximately 7–10 days
★ **V1 distribution, nasal-tip lesions, eye pain** → urgent ophthalmology for zoster ophthalmicus
★ **Ear vesicles + ipsilateral facial paralysis** ± hearing/vestibular symptoms → Ramsay Hunt syndrome
Multiple noncontiguous dermatomes or >20 lesions outside primary/adjacent dermatomes suggests dissemination

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Reduced VZV-specific cellular immunity permits virus to travel from sensory ganglion to skin
Neuronal inflammation/injury explains acute pain and persistent neuropathic symptoms

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Typical eruption → **clinical diagnosis**; atypical lesions → vesicle-base VZV PCR
Assess ocular, neurologic, and systemic findings; consider immunodeficiency evaluation for unusually severe/recurrent disease
CSF PCR for suspected CNS infection; do not delay treatment in high-risk presentations

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Valacyclovir, famciclovir, or acyclovir** ideally within 72 hours; still treat new lesions or complications
Dissemination, visceral/CNS disease, severe immunosuppression → **IV acyclovir**
Acute pain: acetaminophen/NSAID, add neuropathic agent when needed; avoid routine systemic steroids
Ramsay Hunt: antiviral plus glucocorticoid early; eye lubrication/protection for incomplete closure
Postherpetic neuralgia: **gabapentin**/pregabalin, lidocaine patch; TCA anticholinergic in elderly; no late antiviral

rows.label: Complications
items: Persistent pain >90 days, secondary bacterial infection, corneal injury, vision loss
Meningoencephalitis, vasculopathy, visceral spread in vulnerable patients

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Shingrix two doses** for adults ≥50 years or immunocompromised ≥19 years, including prior zoster
Cover lesions, **avoid susceptible contacts** until crusted; exposure causes chickenpox, not immediate shingles
Disseminated: airborne/contact until crusted; immunocompromised localized: same precautions until dissemination excluded

rows.label: Mimics
items: HSV: recurrent localized lesions, often oral/genital rather than a full dermatome
Contact dermatitis: prominent itch, exposure pattern, no neuropathic prodrome

hiv-infection.name: HIV infection
hiv-infection.scope: Acute HIV, testing, ART start, opportunistic infection prophylaxis, PrEP/PEP, opportunistic infections (CMV retinitis, toxoplasmosis, PJP)
hiv-infection.core: HIV progressively depletes CD4 cells; early diagnosis and suppressive ART prevent immune failure and sexual transmission.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Sexual exposure, shared injection equipment, perinatal transmission; other STIs increase acquisition risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Acute infection 2–4 weeks post-exposure: fever, rash, sore throat, **mucosal ulcers**, diarrhea, generalized lymphadenopathy
Weight loss, thrush, recurrent candida/herpes, **extensive adult molluscum** → test HIV; dysphagia → candidal esophagitis
Child/teen: chronic fever/diarrhea, poor growth, generalized nodes, splenomegaly, **polyclonal hypergammaglobulinemia**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Retroviral integration creates lifelong reservoirs; ongoing replication drives immune depletion and inflammation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Fourth-generation Ag/Ab → HIV-1/2 differentiation assay**; discordance → HIV RNA
★ Recent exposure/acute syndrome despite negative screen → **HIV RNA**, before antibodies appear
Baseline viral load, CD4, genotype, renal/liver function, HBV/HCV/TB, pregnancy testing, **cervical cytology**
AIDS: CD4 <200 or AIDS-defining illness regardless of count
Prenatal: opt-out screening; refusal → counsel, re-offer later; never test without consent

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Start **integrase-based ART promptly**, usually bictegravir/TAF/emtricitabine; assess HBV coinfection and interactions
Do not delay routine ART for genotype; cryptococcal/TB meningitis require disease-specific deferred timing
PJP: TMP-SMX; add glucocorticoid if PaO₂ <70 or A–a gradient ≥35
Toxoplasmosis: **pyrimethamine/sulfadiazine/leucovorin**, else TMP-SMX; CMV retinitis: valganciclovir, ophthalmology
Untreated/viremic mother's newborn → **triple ART** ASAP, ideally within 6 h, ≤6 weeks; suppressed mother → zidovudine alone

rows.label: Complications
items: Opportunistic infections, malignancies, wasting, neurocognitive disease, kidney disease
Immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome after ART; drug toxicity/interactions

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ PJP prophylaxis: **TMP-SMX** with CD4 <200 before/starting ART; on ART, <100 or 100–200 with viremia
Toxoplasma IgG positive + CD4 <100 → prophylaxis; MAC <50 only without immediate effective ART
★ Exposure ≤72 hours → **28-day PEP: dolutegravir + TDF/emtricitabine**; do not delay for laboratory results
PrEP: TDF/emtricitabine, cabotegravir, or lenacapavir; exclude HIV first, continue serial testing

rows.label: Mimics
items: EBV mononucleosis: atypical lymphocytes, heterophile positivity; acute HIV can be heterophile-negative
Primary CNS lymphoma: often solitary lesion; biopsy after failed empiric anti-Toxoplasma treatment, earlier if serology/imaging/CSF PCR disagree
SCID/CVID: low immunoglobulins; SCID lymphopenia, no nodes; perinatal HIV: PJP, thrush, nodes, normal lymphocytes

table.title: Advanced-disease syndromes
rows: Dry cough, hypoxemia, ground-glass; sputum/BAL silver stain
Ring-enhancing mass lesions, edema/mass effect; positive IgG
Cognitive decline; non-enhancing subcortical demyelination, no mass effect

hypercalcemia.name: Hypercalcemia
hypercalcemia.scope: Primary hyperparathyroidism, malignancy-associated hypercalcemia, milk-alkali syndrome, IV saline resuscitation, calcitonin, bisphosphonates
hypercalcemia.core: Elevated calcium causes stones, constipation, polyuria, weakness, and neuropsychiatric changes; PTH distinguishes hormone-driven disease from other causes.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Parathyroid adenoma/hyperplasia, malignancy, prolonged immobilization
Thiazides, lithium, excess vitamin D or calcium/absorbable alkali, granulomatous disease

rows.label: Clues
items: Dehydration, nausea, abdominal pain, reduced reflexes; ECG may show shortened QT
★ **Calcium >14 mg/dL**, confusion, arrhythmia, or severe volume depletion → urgent treatment
Primary hyperparathyroidism often asymptomatic; malignancy-associated disease tends to progress rapidly

rows.label: Pathophys
items: PTH promotes bone resorption and renal calcium retention while increasing phosphate excretion
Hypercalcemia impairs renal concentration → dehydration, reduced calcium clearance, self-reinforcing elevation
High filtered calcium exceeds tubular reabsorption → **hypercalciuria** → calcium stones

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Confirm with repeat total/albumin-adjusted or **ionized calcium**, especially with altered proteins or critical illness
★ **Intact PTH first**; elevated or inappropriately normal → PTH-dependent
Suppressed PTH → PTHrP, vitamin D metabolites, malignancy/myeloma evaluation guided by context
Primary disease versus FHH → urine calcium; clearance ratio <0.01 favors FHH, with overlap
Parathyroid imaging localizes before surgery; never establishes biochemical diagnosis

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Severe/symptomatic → **IV isotonic saline**, then calcitonin for rapid temporary lowering
★ **Denosumab** (favored, esp renal limitation/refractory) or **IV zoledronic acid/pamidronate** for sustained malignancy control
Calcitriol-mediated disease → glucocorticoids; dialysis for refractory life-threatening elevation or inability to hydrate
Primary disease: surgery for symptoms, age <50, calcium >1 above ULN, osteoporosis/fracture, stones, eGFR <60
Stop causative supplements/drugs; loop diuretic only for fluid overload, not routine calcium elimination

rows.label: Complications
items: Nephrolithiasis, nephrocalcinosis, AKI, osteoporosis/fractures, pancreatitis
Calcitonin tachyphylaxis after 48–72 hours; antiresorptives can cause hypocalcemia

rows.label: Prevention
items: Hydration, avoid excess calcium/alkali; monitor calcium, renal function, and bone density when observing primary disease

rows.label: Mimics
items: FHH: lifelong mild elevation, family history, hypocalciuria; surgery ineffective
Pseudohypercalcemia: high protein-bound calcium but normal ionized fraction

hypercalcemia.evidence: Not checked online; established calcium evaluation and emergency management.

hyperthyroidism.name: Hyperthyroidism and thyrotoxicosis
hyperthyroidism.scope: Graves disease, toxic multinodular goiter, toxic adenoma, subacute thyroiditis, thyroid storm, beta-blockers, thionamides, radioactive iodine
hyperthyroidism.core: Excess circulating thyroid hormone → heat intolerance, weight loss despite appetite, tremor, and tachycardia; hormone overproduction differs from destructive release.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Autoimmune history, female sex; older age favors autonomous nodules
Iodine load, amiodarone, exogenous thyroid hormone; infection/surgery can precipitate storm

rows.label: Clues
items: Hyperreflexia, lid lag, onycholysis, frequent stools, proximal weakness, widened pulse pressure; older adults: apathetic
★ **Thyroid storm**: fever, delirium, severe tachyarrhythmia, vomiting, heart failure; clinical diagnosis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Increased tissue metabolic activity and beta-adrenergic sensitivity explain systemic manifestations
Thionamides block thyroid peroxidase; PTU also reduces peripheral T4 → T3 conversion

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **TSH first → free T4**, total T3 if T4 normal; suppressed TSH with elevated hormones
TRAb establishes Graves; uncertain cause → **Doppler ultrasound** or radioiodine uptake (not if pregnant/lactating)
Low uptake: thyroiditis/exogenous hormone; low thyroglobulin supports exogenous ingestion

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Symptom control: **propranolol**; caution in asthma or decompensated HF
★ Storm → ICU, cooling/fluids, beta-blockade if tolerated, **PTU → iodine ≥1 hour later**, hydrocortisone
Radioiodine contraindicated during pregnancy/lactation; significant active orbitopathy favors another definitive treatment
Compression/suspicious nodule → thyroidectomy after control; pregnancy: first-trimester PTU, later methimazole

rows.label: Complications
items: AF, embolism, osteoporosis, mild hypercalcemia, cardiomyopathy; radioiodine often → hypothyroidism
★ Thionamides: **fever/sore throat → stop drug, urgent CBC**; PTU → severe hepatotoxicity
Pregnancy: thionamides/TRAb cross placenta → **fetal goiter**, impaired swallowing, polyhydramnios

rows.label: Prevention
items: Monitor free T4 early during treatment; TSH recovery lags
Smoking cessation for orbitopathy; definitive treatment before planned pregnancy when feasible

rows.label: Mimics
items: Panic disorder: episodic symptoms without thyroid biochemical abnormalities
Pheochromocytoma: paroxysmal headache, sweating, severe hypertension
Menopause: hot flashes with menstrual transition, normal thyroid testing
Orbital pseudotumor: involves muscle bellies and tendons; Graves spares tendons

table.title: Etiology determines treatment
rows: Diffuse uptake; bruit, orbitopathy, pretibial myxedema, acropachy (clubbing)
One hot nodule, suppressed surrounding tissue
NSAID; prednisone if severe; no thionamides

hypoglycemia.name: Hypoglycemia
hypoglycemia.scope: Drug-induced hypoglycemia (insulin, sulfonylureas), Whipple triad, acute management (dextrose, glucagon), insulinoma
hypoglycemia.core: Compatible symptoms, documented low plasma glucose, and relief with correction establish Whipple triad and justify evaluation for a hypoglycemic disorder.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Insulin, sulfonylureas; missed meals, exercise, alcohol, kidney failure increase risk
Sepsis, liver failure, adrenal insufficiency; insulinoma causes fasting episodes in otherwise well adults
Child, illness, poor intake or sugar-free fluids → **glycogen depletion**, ketotic hypoglycemia ± anion-gap acidosis

rows.label: Clues
items: Adrenergic: tremor, sweating, palpitations, hunger; neuroglycopenic: confusion, visual change, seizures, coma
Autonomic neuropathy or recurrent episodes may blunt warning symptoms
★ Glucose **<54 mg/dL** clinically significant; diabetes alert threshold <70 mg/dL

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Excess insulin suppresses glucose output and ketones; substrate/hormone deficits impair counterregulation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Bedside glucose immediately**; plasma confirmation if discordant, never delay emergency correction
Critical sample: glucose, insulin, C-peptide, proinsulin, β-hydroxybutyrate, sulfonylurea screen
Suspected endogenous fasting disorder → supervised fast up to 72 h; mixed-meal test for postprandial symptoms
Biochemically confirmed insulinoma → pancreatic CT/MRI, endoscopic ultrasound if localization unclear

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Awake and swallowing → **15 g rapid carbohydrate**, recheck after 15 minutes, repeat if needed
★ Altered or unable to swallow → **IV dextrose**; no IV access → IM/intranasal glucagon
After recovery → longer-acting carbohydrate; glucagon less effective after alcohol or glycogen depletion
★ Sulfonylurea recurrence → **octreotide + dextrose**, prolonged observation; long-acting insulin may require infusion
Adjust diabetes regimen and treat trigger; localized insulinoma → surgical resection

rows.label: Complications
items: Seizures, brain injury, arrhythmias, falls; recurrent episodes cause impaired awareness
Dextrose alone after sulfonylurea exposure may stimulate further insulin release

rows.label: Prevention
items: Meal/exercise planning, glucose monitoring or CGM alarms, caregiver rescue-glucagon education
Relax overly intensive targets when recurrent events, frailty, or impaired awareness

rows.label: Mimics
items: Panic attack: normal glucose during symptoms
Stroke: focal deficit may persist after glucose correction; evaluate both if unresolved

hypoglycemia.evidence: Not checked online; established endocrine diagnostic and hypoglycemia treatment principles.

hypothesis-testing-and-statistical-tests.name: Hypothesis testing and statistical tests
hypothesis-testing-and-statistical-tests.scope: Null and alternative hypotheses, Type I and Type II errors, statistical power, confidence intervals, p-values, t-tests (paired, unpaired), ANOVA, chi-square, Pearson correlation
hypothesis-testing-and-statistical-tests.core: Hypothesis tests quantify incompatibility with a null model; confidence intervals describe effect estimates and uncertainty.

rows.label: Definition
items: H0: no difference/association; H1: specified difference or association
★ **α**: false-positive probability; Type I error rejects a true null
★ **β**: false-negative probability; Type II error misses a real effect

rows.label: Formula
items: Power = **1 − β**; increases with sample size, effect size, α, lower variability
95% CI ≈ estimate ± 1.96 × standard error; plausible range for true effect

rows.label: Interpret
items: ★ **p-value**: probability of equally/more extreme data assuming H0; not probability H0 true
95% CI excludes 0 for differences or 1 for ratios → two-sided p <0.05

rows.label: Use when
items: Pearson r: linear association between continuous variables; range −1 to +1
Ordinal/non-normal independent data → Mann–Whitney; paired → Wilcoxon signed-rank

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Nonsignificant ≠ equivalent; statistical significance ≠ clinical importance
Repeated comparisons inflate false positives; prespecify outcomes or adjust α
Correlation neither establishes causation nor detects every nonlinear relationship

hypothesis-testing-and-statistical-tests.evidence: Statistical definitions; no clinical guideline involved.

impaired-physician.name: Impaired physician
impaired-physician.scope: Acute impairment, substance use, patient safety protection, physician health programs, mandatory reporting to state medical board
impaired-physician.core: Patient safety first when a colleague's ability to practice safely is compromised.

rows.label: Principle
items: Impairment = functional inability to practice safely from illness, substances, or cognitive decline

rows.label: Do
items: ★ Acute intoxication → stop patient contact, arrange coverage, notify supervisor immediately
★ Document objective observations and affected encounters through institutional channels
★ **Physician health program** → evaluation, treatment, monitoring, and safe return to practice

rows.label: Don't
items: Conceal unsafe care or delay intervention while seeking definitive proof
Permit impaired colleague to drive home

rows.label: Exceptions
items: ★ Report to **state medical board** when law requires or ongoing danger remains unaddressed
PHP confidentiality and reporting exemptions vary by jurisdiction

rows.label: Traps
items: Substance use history or treatment alone ≠ current impairment
Employee assistance referral alone insufficient during an immediate patient safety threat

impaired-physician.evidence: Checked AMA Code of Medical Ethics Opinion 9.3.2.

infant-nutrition.name: Infant nutrition
infant-nutrition.scope: Exclusive breastfeeding recommendations, vitamin D supplementation, introduction of solid foods, cow milk protein allergy (hydrolyzed formula), formula types
infant-nutrition.core: Breast milk or iron-fortified infant formula anchors first-year nutrition; add supplements and complementary foods according to developmental readiness.

rows.label: Who
items: All infants; assess growth, feeding effectiveness, urine output, and family feeding preferences

rows.label: Schedule
items: ★ **Exclusive breastfeeding about 6 months**; continue with complementary foods through 2 years or longer
★ Solids around **6 months**, never before 4; head control, sitting, diminished extrusion reflex
Begin iron-rich meat or fortified cereal; advance textures; introduce allergens without unnecessary delay

rows.label: Special groups
items: ★ Breastfed/partially breastfed → **vitamin D 400 IU/day** from shortly after birth
Formula-only: vitamin D supplement until intake ≥32 oz/day
Exclusively breastfed term infants: **iron 1 mg/kg/day from 4 months** until adequate dietary iron

rows.label: Choice
items: Blood-streaked stool, eczema, emesis → milk-protein allergy; confirm elimination/rechallenge
Breastfed proctocolitis → maternal dairy elimination, dietitian; persistent symptoms → eliminate soy
Proctocolitis: non-IgE, usually outgrown by age 1–3; lactose intolerance: no bloody stool

rows.label: Contraindications
items: No **honey before 12 months**; avoid choking hazards and unpasteurized foods
No cow milk as primary drink before 12 months; no homemade/diluted formula
Classic galactosemia → avoid breast milk and lactose-containing formula

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Lactose-free ≠ hypoallergenic**; avoid partial hydrolysates/goat milk for milk-protein allergy
Severe eczema/egg allergy → peanut evaluation and introduction at 4–6 months
No cereal in bottles; responsive feeding, no forced finishing

infectious-mononucleosis.name: Infectious mononucleosis
infectious-mononucleosis.scope: Epstein-Barr virus, triad of fever, pharyngitis, lymphadenopathy, atypical lymphocytes, heterophile antibody test, splenic rupture precautions
infectious-mononucleosis.core: An adolescent or young adult with fever, exudative pharyngitis, posterior cervical lymphadenopathy, and prolonged fatigue likely has EBV mononucleosis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Salivary transmission, close intimate contact, shared drink containers; primary symptomatic infection often in adolescence
Immunocompromised patients face greater risk of EBV-related lymphoproliferative disease

rows.label: Clues
items: Palatal petechiae, generalized nodes, splenomegaly, mild hepatomegaly/transaminase elevation
★ **Atypical lymphocytes** on smear; reactive cells are CD8 T lymphocytes, not infected B cells
★ Diffuse rash after **amoxicillin/ampicillin** supports EBV; not automatically lifelong penicillin allergy
Severe tonsillar enlargement with stridor/drooling → assess airway immediately

rows.label: Pathophys
items: EBV infects B cells via CD21; cytotoxic immune response produces systemic symptoms and lymphocytosis
Reticuloendothelial expansion enlarges spleen and weakens its capsule

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Heterophile antibody test** with CBC in typical presentation
False negatives early in illness and in young children → EBV-specific serology
Acute infection: VCA IgM positive with absent EBNA; EBNA develops later and persists
Mononucleosis-like illness with negative EBV tests → consider CMV and acute HIV testing

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Hydration, rest, acetaminophen/NSAID, viscous lidocaine gargle**; gradual activity as symptoms improve
No routine antibiotics, antivirals, or glucocorticoids for uncomplicated disease
Steroids only for threatened airway or severe immune complications, such as hemolysis/thrombocytopenia
Sudden LUQ pain, referred left shoulder pain, syncope → urgent splenic rupture evaluation and resuscitation

rows.label: Complications
items: Splenic rupture, airway obstruction, autoimmune hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia
Hepatitis, prolonged fatigue; rare neurologic involvement; avoid alcohol during significant liver inflammation

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **No athletic activity for first 3 weeks** from onset; then light noncontact activity if recovered
Contact/collision sports and heavy lifting deferred until recovery and individualized clearance; usually ≥3–4 weeks
No routine ultrasound solely to clear athletes; avoid sharing saliva-contaminated objects

rows.label: Mimics
items: Streptococcal pharyngitis: anterior nodes, no typical atypical lymphocytosis or splenic enlargement
CMV: heterophile-negative syndrome, less prominent pharyngitis
Acute HIV: exposure history, rash/mucosal ulcers; antigen/antibody plus RNA testing

infective-endocarditis.name: Infective endocarditis
infective-endocarditis.scope: Native and prosthetic valve endocarditis, Duke criteria, prophylaxis, IV drug use endocarditis, blood culture diagnostic criteria
infective-endocarditis.core: Persistent bacteremia with valve infection causes systemic emboli, valve destruction, and immune-complex injury.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prosthetic valve, prior endocarditis, congenital valve abnormality, intracardiac device
Injection drug use → tricuspid involvement; healthcare exposure, indwelling vascular access

rows.label: Clues
items: Fever, new regurgitant murmur, embolic stroke, splenic infarct, hematuria
Janeway lesions painless; Osler nodes painful; Roth spots retinal; splinter hemorrhages nonspecific
★ **New conduction block** → periannular abscess; right-sided disease → septic pulmonary emboli

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Endothelial injury → platelet-fibrin nidus → microbial adherence and vegetation
Immune complexes → glomerulonephritis; infected fragments disseminate through downstream circulation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Three blood-culture sets before antibiotics**; separate peripheral draws unless resuscitation would be delayed
Major microbiology: **typical organism in ≥2 culture sets**, nontypical in ≥3; specialized serology/PCR also qualifies
★ **TTE → TEE** if prosthesis/high suspicion; major imaging: vegetation, abscess, perforation, new significant regurgitation
Definite clinical Duke: 2 major, 1 major + 3 minor, or 5 minor criteria
Minor: predisposition, fever, vascular phenomena, immunologic phenomena, nondiagnostic microbiology

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Empiric **IV vancomycin + cefepime** for acutely ill/healthcare-associated cases; tailor to cultures and setting
MSSA → nafcillin/oxacillin or cefazolin; susceptible viridans streptococci → ceftriaxone
Prolonged pathogen-directed IV antibiotics; prosthetic infections need specialist regimen and early surgical evaluation
Surgery: heart failure, abscess, persistent bacteremia, fungal infection, or selected recurrent/large embolizing vegetations

rows.label: Complications
items: Acute regurgitation, heart failure, mycotic aneurysm, metastatic infection
Antibiotic nephrotoxicity, line infection; hemorrhage into embolic cerebral lesions

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Dental **amoxicillin** for prosthetic valve/material, previous IE, selected cyanotic/residual CHD, transplant valvulopathy
Good oral hygiene, sterile access; no routine prophylaxis for GI/GU procedures or isolated MVP

rows.label: Mimics
items: Nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis: cancer/autoimmune disease, sterile cultures
Atrial myxoma: positional obstruction, intracavitary mass; vasculitis: no infected vegetation

inflammatory-bowel-disease.name: Inflammatory bowel disease
inflammatory-bowel-disease.scope: Crohn disease, ulcerative colitis, extraintestinal manifestations (erythema nodosum, pyoderma gangrenosum, uveitis), toxic megacolon, colorectal cancer risk, biologic therapy
inflammatory-bowel-disease.core: Chronic relapsing intestinal inflammation: Crohn disease affects any gastrointestinal segment; ulcerative colitis begins in the rectum.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Family history, young adulthood; smoking worsens Crohn disease
NSAIDs and enteric infections can precipitate flares

rows.label: Clues
items: Chronic diarrhea, abdominal pain, weight loss, anemia; children may have growth failure
Arthritis, uveitis; PSC particularly associated with UC
Erythema nodosum: tender nonulcerating nodules; **pyoderma gangrenosum**: rapid painful violaceous ulcer, purulent base
★ Severe colitis: fever, tachycardia, frequent bloody stools; distention, colon >6 cm → **toxic megacolon**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Dysregulated mucosal immune response to intestinal microbiota in genetically susceptible hosts

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Stool **C. difficile** testing and cultures before attributing worsening diarrhea to inflammation
Fecal calprotectin supports intestinal inflammation; **ileocolonoscopy with biopsies** confirms
Suspected small-bowel disease or abscess → CT/MR enterography; avoid capsule with suspected stricture
Partial SBO, suspected stricture → enterography; older exam questions may expect **water-soluble small-bowel follow-through**
Fulminant colitis → abdominal radiograph and limited sigmoidoscopy; avoid full colonoscopy

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Acute severe UC → hospitalization, **IV methylprednisolone**, fluids, VTE prophylaxis
Steroid-refractory severe UC → infliximab or cyclosporine; perforation or megacolon → urgent colectomy
★ Moderate/severe flare without obstruction or abscess → **prednisone** induces remission only; **never maintenance**
Crohn abscess → antibiotics and drainage before immunosuppression
UC with colorectal cancer → **total proctocolectomy**, not segmental colectomy

rows.label: Complications
items: Fistulas (enterovaginal → vaginal flatus), strictures, obstruction in Crohn; colectomy does not cure Crohn
Terminal ileal Crohn → B12 deficiency, **bile salt malabsorption** → steatorrhea
Colonic disease → colorectal cancer; active inflammation → venous thromboembolism

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Colonic disease → surveillance colonoscopy beginning about **8 years** after onset; PSC → immediately
Vaccinate and screen TB/HBV before biologics; smoking cessation for Crohn

rows.label: Mimics
items: IBS: no bleeding, weight loss or inflammatory markers
Ischemic colitis: abrupt pain followed by hematochezia, vascular risk

table.title: Distribution and outpatient treatment
rows: RLQ mass, cobblestones, perianal disease, granulomas
Bloody diarrhea, tenesmus; friability, crypt abscesses, pseudopolyps

informed-consent-and-capacity.name: Informed consent and capacity
informed-consent-and-capacity.scope: Decision-making capacity, informed consent, emergency exception (implied consent), refusal of treatment, AMA discharge
informed-consent-and-capacity.core: A capable adult may accept or refuse treatment after understanding its benefits, material risks, alternatives, and consequences of refusal.

rows.label: Principle
items: ★ Capacity: **understand, appreciate (own case), reason, communicate**; decision-specific, fluctuating
Competence: legal; diagnosis, age, alcohol use, incarceration, disagreement alone ≠ incapacity

rows.label: Do
items: ★ Explain benefits, material risks, alternatives/no treatment; **qualified interpreter and teach-back**
Correct delirium, intoxication, pain, communication barriers; reassess capacity
AMA request: assess capacity, explore barriers, offer safer plan, document discussion and follow-up

rows.label: Don't
items: Capable refusal → respect choice, even if life-saving or pregnant; avoid coercion, abandonment
No valid consent → possible **battery**; signed form alone insufficient
Refusing one therapy (blood) ≠ refusing all; provide other indicated care, including surgery

rows.label: Exceptions
items: ★ Emergency + incapacity + no surrogate/directive/verified refusal → implied consent to treat
★ Parents refuse minor's life-saving transfusion → **treat emergency**; seek court authority if feasible
Incapacity without emergency → authorized surrogate; involve patient to remaining ability

rows.label: Traps
items: Psychiatric illness does not automatically remove capacity; assess the specific decision
Suicide danger may justify protective detention despite expressed desire to leave
New material procedure or changed risk → renewed consent; consent revocable anytime before procedure

table.title: Who decides
rows: Ask whom to involve; facilitate promptly; no override
Minor decides; no parental consent (state law varies)
Parents seek unproven remedy for child
Continue proven therapy; investigate remedy; CPS not first
Close; discuss after waking; no next-of-kin consent
Autonomy ≠ entitlement; physician refuses, explains, offers alternatives

informed-consent-and-capacity.evidence: Not checked online; established consent/capacity ethics; emergency and minor-consent law varies by jurisdiction.

inguinal-hernia.name: Inguinal hernia
inguinal-hernia.scope: Direct inguinal hernia, indirect inguinal hernia, femoral hernia, incarcerated and strangulated hernia, physical exam, elective vs emergent surgical repair
inguinal-hernia.core: A groin bulge enlarging with strain suggests hernia; a painful irreducible mass with obstructive or ischemic signs requires urgent surgical assessment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Male sex, family history, prematurity, persistent processus vaginalis
Age-related fascial weakness, chronic cough, constipation, heavy strain; femoral hernias more frequent in women

rows.label: Clues
items: Bulge or dragging discomfort with standing/Valsalva, improving supine or after reduction
Incarcerated: contents cannot be reduced; bowel obstruction causes vomiting, distention, obstipation
★ **Severe persistent pain**, tenderness, erythema, toxicity/peritonitis → impaired perfusion; fever may be late

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Abdominal contents protrude through a weak opening; a narrow neck impairs venous then arterial perfusion
Richter hernia traps only bowel-wall segment; ischemia may occur without complete obstruction

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Standing groin examination with cough/Valsalva**; inspect both sides and assess reducibility
Uncertain occult lesion → dynamic ultrasound; CT if obstruction, complication, or alternative diagnosis suspected
Clinical strangulation → immediate operation; imaging must not delay treatment
Do not rely on surface examination alone to reliably distinguish direct from indirect anatomy

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Strangulation → **IV fluids, NPO, analgesia, antibiotics, emergency repair**; resect nonviable bowel
Incarceration without ischemic features → urgent surgeon evaluation; gentle reduction only in selected cases
★ Symptomatic inguinal hernia → **elective mesh repair** in adults; children → herniotomy
Minimally symptomatic men may choose watchful waiting with return precautions
Women and femoral hernias → timely repair because occult femoral disease and strangulation risk are greater

rows.label: Complications
items: Bowel obstruction, ischemic necrosis, perforation, sepsis
Repair → chronic groin pain, recurrence, wound/mesh infection, testicular ischemia

rows.label: Prevention
items: Treat constipation and chronic cough, smoking cessation, weight management; risk reduction cannot close an existing defect
After reduction or observation: urgent return for escalating pain, vomiting, or loss of reducibility

rows.label: Mimics
items: Lymphadenopathy: discrete solid nodes without cough impulse
Hydrocele: transilluminates; confined fluid rather than reducible bowel
Saphena varix: compressible venous swelling; Doppler demonstrates venous flow

table.title: Anatomic distinctions
rows: Below inguinal ligament, medial femoral vein

inherited-bleeding-disorders.name: Inherited bleeding disorders
inherited-bleeding-disorders.scope: Hemophilia A, Hemophilia B, von Willebrand disease, factor XI deficiency, hemarthrosis, mixing studies, factor VIII inhibitors
inherited-bleeding-disorders.core: Deep tissue bleeding suggests a coagulation-factor defect; mucosal bleeding suggests platelet/von Willebrand dysfunction, even with a normal platelet count.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Hemophilia A/B: X-linked, usually males; maternal family history may be absent
vWD usually autosomal dominant; factor XI deficiency autosomal, enriched in Ashkenazi ancestry

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Recurrent **hemarthroses**, muscle hematomas and delayed postoperative bleeding → hemophilia
Epistaxis, gingival bleeding, easy bruising and heavy menses → vWD
Factor XI deficiency: variable postsurgical bleeding, especially oral/urologic procedures; hemarthrosis uncommon
Unexpected major bleeding after circumcision or surgery may reveal previously undiagnosed disease

rows.label: Pathophys
items: VIII/IX/XI deficits impair intrinsic-pathway thrombin generation and fibrin stabilization
vWF mediates platelet adhesion and stabilizes factor VIII; deficiency impairs primary and sometimes secondary hemostasis

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ CBC/platelets, PT, aPTT; **mixing study corrects** factor deficiency, fails with inhibitor
Factor VIII, IX or XI activity identifies deficiency; hemophilia generally normal PT/platelets
★ Suspected vWD → **vWF antigen, activity and factor VIII**; aPTT may be normal
Stress, pregnancy and estrogen raise vWF; repeat borderline testing when clinically stable
Severe hemophilia: factor activity <1%; inhibitor testing if replacement response is inadequate

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Major suspected hemophilic bleeding → **replace deficient factor immediately**, before imaging delays
Hemophilia A → factor VIII; B → factor IX; emicizumab prophylaxis for selected A
Mild responsive A or type 1 vWD → **desmopressin after response testing**
Severe vWD → vWF-containing concentrate; avoid desmopressin in type 2B and ineffective type 3
Mucosal bleeding → tranexamic acid; factor XI procedures → antifibrinolytic ± plasma with hematology planning

rows.label: Complications
items: Chronic hemarthropathy, intracranial hemorrhage, anemia; factor inhibitors complicate replacement
Desmopressin → water retention/hyponatremia; factor concentrates can increase thrombosis risk

rows.label: Prevention
items: Individualized factor/nonfactor prophylaxis, dental care, procedure planning; avoid aspirin and nonselective NSAIDs
Family genetic counseling; fluid restriction and sodium monitoring around desmopressin

rows.label: Mimics
items: ITP: low platelets with mucocutaneous bleeding
Acquired factor VIII inhibitor: new bleeding, mixing fails to correct
Vitamin K deficiency: PT prolonged first

interstitial-lung-disease.name: Interstitial lung disease
interstitial-lung-disease.scope: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, hypersensitivity pneumonitis, sarcoidosis, pneumoconioses, restrictive PFTs (reduced DLCO, normal/high FEV1/FVC), high-resolution CT
interstitial-lung-disease.core: Progressive exertional dyspnea, dry cough, and inspiratory crackles suggest diffuse parenchymal lung disease; HRCT patterns and exposure history identify the cause.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Age >60 and smoking: IPF; autoimmune disease; familial fibrosis
Amiodarone, bleomycin, nitrofurantoin; occupational silica/coal/asbestos, organic antigens; prior thoracic radiation

rows.label: Clues
items: Fine basal Velcro crackles, exertional desaturation, later clubbing; systemic rheumatic features can reveal cause
Sarcoidosis: bilateral hilar adenopathy, uveitis, erythema nodosum, sometimes hypercalcemia
Rapidly worsening oxygenation → infection, embolism, edema, or acute exacerbation evaluation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Alveolar/interstitial injury and aberrant repair reduce lung compliance and gas-transfer capacity
Granulomatous inflammation or fibrogenic dust responses produce distinct imaging distributions

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **HRCT + full PFTs** after chest radiograph; obtain detailed drug, occupation, hobby, autoimmune history
★ **↓TLC, ↓DLCO, normal/↑FEV1/FVC** support restriction; low FVC alone is insufficient
UIP: basal subpleural reticulation, traction bronchiectasis, honeycombing; exclude known causes before labeling IPF
Autoantibodies when connective-tissue disease suspected; BAL/biopsy selected through multidisciplinary review
Typical UIP without secondary cause may avoid surgical biopsy; assess exertional oxygen needs

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Remove offending exposure/drug**, pulmonary rehabilitation, oxygen for hypoxemia; treat identified cause
★ IPF: **nintedanib or pirfenidone** slows decline; no routine chronic prednisone-based immunosuppression
Inflammatory sarcoid/autoimmune disease: selected steroids or steroid-sparing agents; mild sarcoid may need observation
Progressive fibrotic non-IPF disease → nintedanib consideration; advanced disease → early transplant evaluation

rows.label: Complications
items: Pulmonary hypertension, cor pulmonale, respiratory failure, exacerbations; asbestos raises lung cancer/mesothelioma risk
Silicosis increases TB susceptibility; antifibrotics can cause GI adverse effects and liver injury

rows.label: Prevention
items: Smoking cessation, respiratory immunizations, occupational dust controls, medication monitoring; follow FVC/DLCO trends

rows.label: Mimics
items: Heart failure: congestion/cardiomegaly, volume response; emphysema: obstruction with hyperinflation
Neuromuscular restriction: low volumes with relatively preserved diffusion capacity

table.title: Imaging clues to etiology
rows: Centrilobular nodules, mosaic attenuation, air trapping

intrapartum-fetal-monitoring.name: Intrapartum fetal monitoring
intrapartum-fetal-monitoring.scope: Baseline fetal heart rate, variability, early decelerations, late decelerations, variable decelerations, category I II III tracings, intrauterine resuscitation
intrapartum-fetal-monitoring.core: Fetal oxygenation assessment from baseline, variability, and decelerations; persistent category III requires expedited delivery after immediate resuscitation.

rows.label: Definition
items: ★ Normal baseline **110–160/min**; moderate variability **6–25 beats/min**
Bradycardia <110; tachycardia >160; baseline change lasts ≥10 minutes
Tachysystole: >5 contractions/10 minutes over 30 minutes; oxytocin excess → late decelerations

rows.label: Interpret
items: Early: mirrors contraction → head compression; benign
Late: nadir after contraction peak → uteroplacental insufficiency
Variable: abrupt fall → cord compression; prolonged: 2–10 minutes

rows.label: Use when
items: ★ Category II: lateral positioning, stop oxytocin, IV fluids; correct hypotension
Persistent tachysystole with concerning tracing → **terbutaline**; recurrent variables → amnioinfusion
★ Bradycardia: exam for cord prolapse; post-epidural → **maternal hypotension**; prepare delivery

rows.label: Compare
items: **Maternal fever** commonest tachycardia, variability kept; hypoxia → low variability, late decelerations
Transient minimal variability, no decelerations → **fetal sleep**, usually <40 minutes
Late decelerations → hypoxemia → **metabolic acidosis**; acute cord compression → respiratory acidosis

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Oxygen only for **maternal hypoxemia**; older routine-oxygen answers conflict with current guidance
Moderate variability or accelerations strongly argues against current metabolic acidemia
Category II alone does not mandate cesarean; reassess response and labor progress

table.title: Three-tier interpretation
rows: Reassuring rate/variability; no late or variable decelerations
Absent variability + recurrent late/variable decelerations or bradycardia
Resuscitate; unresolved → cesarean unless fully dilated
Evaluate severe anemia; expedite if persistent

irritable-bowel-syndrome.name: Irritable bowel syndrome
irritable-bowel-syndrome.scope: Rome IV criteria, IBS subtypes (IBS-C, IBS-D, IBS-M), alarm features, low FODMAP diet, antispasmodics, fiber supplementation
irritable-bowel-syndrome.core: Recurrent abdominal pain linked to defecation and altered stool frequency/form, without alarm findings, supports a positive diagnosis of IBS.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Younger age, female sex, anxiety/depression, adverse life stress, previous enteric infection
Food-related symptom flares common; psychosocial associations do not make symptoms imaginary

rows.label: Clues
items: **Cramps relieved by defecation**, sometimes worsened; bloating, urgency, mucus, incomplete evacuation
★ **Bleeding, anemia, weight loss, fever, nocturnal diarrhea**, family cancer/IBD history → evaluate organic disease
New onset in older adults warrants careful assessment and age-based colorectal cancer screening

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Disordered gut–brain signaling, visceral/smooth-muscle hypersensitivity, altered motility and microbiome contribute
No destructive mucosal inflammation; subtype follows predominant abnormal stool consistency

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Rome IV**: pain ≥1 day/week over prior 3 months, symptom onset ≥6 months earlier
At least two: related to defecation, change in stool frequency, change in stool form
CBC; diarrhea phenotype → celiac serology and fecal calprotectin/lactoferrin ± CRP when no alarms
★ **No routine colonoscopy** in younger patients meeting criteria without warning signs or screening indication
Review medications, lactose intolerance, infectious exposures; stool pathogen tests only when suggested by history

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Soluble fiber/psyllium**, regular meals, exercise; limited low-FODMAP trial with structured reintroduction
Gut-directed CBT/hypnotherapy; peppermint oil may help pain; TCA useful for persistent pain, especially diarrhea
Dicyclomine: selected episodic cramping; anticholinergic harms, weak global-symptom evidence; avoid routine use

rows.label: Complications
items: Quality-of-life impairment, restrictive diets, anxiety; no increased colorectal cancer risk from IBS itself
Eluxadoline: pancreatitis risk, contraindicated without gallbladder; avoid escalating opioids

rows.label: Prevention
items: Identify dietary/stress triggers, maintain activity; avoid prolonged unnecessary elimination diets
Reassess new alarm findings rather than attributing every symptom to established IBS

rows.label: Mimics
items: IBD: objective inflammation/bleeding; celiac: positive serology, malabsorption
Microscopic colitis: watery nocturnal diarrhea, normal-looking colon, diagnostic biopsies

table.title: Stool subtype and targeted treatment
rows: PEG for constipation; linaclotide/lubiprostone for global symptoms
Loperamide for diarrhea; rifaximin for global symptoms

ischemic-stroke-and-tia.name: Ischemic stroke and TIA
ischemic-stroke-and-tia.scope: TIA (including amaurosis fugax), ischemic stroke, acute management (tPA, thrombectomy), secondary prevention, risk factors
ischemic-stroke-and-tia.core: Abrupt focal neurologic loss from cerebral ischemia; transient monocular blindness means retinal embolism from the ipsilateral carotid.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: ★ **Hypertension: greatest modifiable risk factor**; smoking, diabetes, dyslipidemia, carotid atherosclerosis
Atrial fibrillation, recent MI, endocarditis, arterial dissection

rows.label: Clues
items: **Broca** nonfluent, poor repetition, intact comprehension; **Wernicke** fluent paraphasias, poor comprehension, no insight
Crossed: **Weber** ipsilateral CN III, contralateral hemiparesis (midbrain); lateral pons: ipsilateral full-face palsy, deafness
★ **Last known well** establishes treatment timing; symptom discovery time may differ
TIA: resolved deficit without acute infarction, often embolic; urgent evaluation despite normal examination

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Thromboembolism or small-vessel occlusion → infarct core surrounded by salvageable penumbra
Reperfusion preserves threatened tissue but increases hemorrhagic transformation risk

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Fingerstick glucose + **noncontrast head CT** first; normal early CT does not exclude ischemia
CTA head/neck for large-vessel occlusion; MRI diffusion for small infarcts or diagnostic uncertainty
ECG, telemetry, carotid imaging; echocardiography for suspected cardiac emboli

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Disabling deficit, eligible ≤4.5 hours → **alteplase or tenecteplase**; imaging-selected extended windows possible
Thrombolysis: BP <185/110 before, <180/105 after; exclude bleeding and significant anticoagulant effect
★ Large-vessel occlusion → **mechanical thrombectomy**, selected cases through 24 hours; do not delay thrombolysis
No reperfusion: generally allow BP ≤220/120; oxygen for hypoxemia; swallow assessment before oral intake
Aspirin after hemorrhage excluded; after thrombolysis, wait 24 hours and repeat imaging

rows.label: Complications
items: Cerebral edema, aspiration, venous thrombosis, seizures, disability

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Minor noncardioembolic stroke/high-risk TIA → short **aspirin + clopidogrel**, then single antiplatelet
AF/cardioembolic → oral anticoagulation, timing by infarct/bleeding risk; noncardioembolic → antiplatelet only
Symptomatic carotid stenosis 70–99% → endarterectomy when eligible; selected 50–69% also benefit
Long-term antiplatelet (aspirin allergy → clopidogrel); undertreated hypertension → **intensify antihypertensives**; high-intensity statin

rows.label: Mimics
items: Hypoglycemia: deficit reverses with glucose
Migraine aura: spreading positive symptoms; seizure: witnessed convulsion followed by Todd paralysis

table.title: Vascular localization
rows: Occipital: contralateral homonymous hemianopia; macular sparing
Diplopia, vertigo, dysarthria, ataxia, crossed/bilateral signs, coma
Vertigo; ipsilateral Horner/face/ataxia/palate; contralateral body pain-temperature

kawasaki-disease.name: Kawasaki disease
kawasaki-disease.scope: Diagnostic criteria (CRASH and burn), echocardiography, coronary artery aneurysms, intravenous immunoglobulin, aspirin, refractory disease
kawasaki-disease.core: Persistent fever with mucocutaneous inflammation in a young child suggests Kawasaki disease; early treatment reduces coronary artery injury.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Usually age <5 years; more common in children of East Asian ancestry
Infants, delayed diagnosis, and early coronary abnormalities increase complication risk

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Fever ≥5 days + ≥4 CRASH features**; experienced clinicians may diagnose earlier when classic
C: bilateral nonpurulent conjunctivitis; R: polymorphous rash; A: cervical adenopathy, usually unilateral >1.5 cm
S: oral strawberry tongue/cracked red lips; H: hand/foot erythema/edema → later periungual peeling
Irritability, sterile pyuria, ↑ESR/CRP; thrombocytosis typically after first week, not required initially

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Immune-mediated medium-vessel vasculitis preferentially injures coronary arteries
Inflammation weakens arterial walls → dilation/aneurysm, thrombosis, and later stenosis

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical diagnosis + echocardiography** at presentation; normal initial echo does not exclude disease
Prolonged unexplained fever with 2–3 features, especially infant → incomplete-disease inflammatory/echo algorithm
CBC, CRP/ESR, albumin, liver tests, urinalysis support assessment; no single confirmatory laboratory test
Repeat echo at approximately 1–2 and 4–6 weeks; more frequent for coronary abnormalities

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **IVIG + aspirin promptly**, ideally within first 10 days; treat later if ongoing inflammation/coronary disease
Acute anti-inflammatory aspirin → low-dose antiplatelet phase after afebrile; duration follows coronary findings
★ High-risk disease → consider **adjunct glucocorticoids** with initial IVIG through specialist team
Fever ≥36 hours after IVIG → reassess; repeat IVIG, infliximab, or steroids for refractory disease
Large/giant aneurysms → additional anticoagulation with cardiology; manage shock/myocarditis supportively

rows.label: Complications
items: Coronary aneurysm, thrombosis, MI → ischemic heart failure; myocarditis, ventricular dysfunction, valvular regurgitation
IVIG can cause hemolysis; aspirin increases bleeding and Reye risk during influenza/varicella

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ After IVIG, **delay MMR/varicella approximately 11 months**; maintain cardiology follow-up
Annual inactivated influenza vaccination while receiving aspirin; promptly discuss varicella exposure

rows.label: Mimics
items: Adenovirus: exudative conjunctivitis/pharyngitis; scarlet fever: positive streptococcal testing, no coronary involvement
MIS-C: recent SARS-CoV-2, older child, marked GI symptoms/shock, often thrombocytopenia
DRESS: recent drug, weeks' latency, facial edema, eosinophilia, hepatitis; conjunctivitis/strawberry tongue favor Kawasaki

knee-injuries.name: Knee injuries
knee-injuries.scope: Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) tear, posterior cruciate ligament (PCL) tear, collateral ligaments, meniscal tears, knee dislocation, popliteal artery injury, Ottawa knee rules
knee-injuries.core: Knee trauma assessment starts with neurovascular safety and fracture risk, then uses mechanism, effusion timing, and targeted ligament or meniscal tests.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Pivoting/cutting sports, contact trauma, dashboard impact, hyperextension
Older age, osteoporosis, and inability to bear weight increase fracture probability

rows.label: Clues
items: Immediate large effusion suggests hemarthrosis; delayed swelling and catching suggest meniscal injury
★ **Gross deformity or spontaneously reduced dislocation** → popliteal artery injury risk
Cool foot, weak pulses, paresthesia, escalating pain → vascular compromise or compartment syndrome

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Ligament disruption → instability; displaced meniscal fragment → mechanical locking
Knee dislocation may stretch/tear popliteal artery despite restored alignment and initially palpable pulses

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Neurovascular examination before and after reduction**; ABI assesses arterial injury
★ ABI **<0.9, abnormal pulses, or pre-reduction deficit → CT angiography**; hard ischemic signs → vascular intervention
Normal ABI/pulses, no prior deficit → serial vascular checks, not immediate discharge
Ottawa: age ≥55, isolated patellar/fibular-head tenderness, flexion <90°, or inability four-step weight-bearing → radiographs
MRI for soft-tissue injury after fracture evaluation; locked knee → prompt orthopedic assessment

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Dislocation → **urgent reduction before angiography**, immobilization, orthopedic/vascular consultation
Initial sprain → ice/compression, analgesia, protected weight bearing then early rehabilitation
Isolated collateral sprain → hinged brace + rehabilitation; many PCL injuries managed nonoperatively
ACL rupture with athletic demands/persistent instability or combined injury → reconstruction discussion
Displaced locked meniscal tear → arthroscopy; degenerative tears without locking usually exercise-based rehabilitation

rows.label: Complications
items: Missed arterial injury → limb loss; peroneal nerve injury → foot drop
Chronic instability, recurrent meniscal injury, posttraumatic osteoarthritis, stiffness

rows.label: Prevention
items: Neuromuscular landing/pivot training, strength and balance rehabilitation before sport return

rows.label: Mimics
items: Patellar dislocation: lateral patellar displacement, often spontaneous reduction
Septic arthritis: atraumatic hot effusion, fever; urgent aspiration
Patellofemoral pain/instability: running, stairs, sitting → anterior pain; crepitus, genu valgum, lax patella; no effusion unless acute dislocation
Osgood-Schlatter: growth-spurt athlete, chronic tibial tubercle pain; traction apophysitis, tendon-insertion microfractures

table.title: Mechanism and examination
rows: Joint-line tenderness; McMurray: click on rotation/extension; Thessaly

knee-injuries.evidence: Not checked online; established orthopedic trauma and Ottawa knee principles.

low-back-pain.name: Low back pain
low-back-pain.scope: Lumbosacral strain, herniated disk and radiculopathy, spinal stenosis, red flags, imaging indications, conservative management
low-back-pain.core: Most acute low back pain improves with activity and analgesia; neurologic deficits or systemic red flags change the workup.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Heavy lifting, deconditioning, obesity, prolonged sitting
Cancer, immunosuppression, injection drug use, osteoporosis, chronic glucocorticoids increase serious-pathology risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Mechanical pain varies with movement; isolated axial pain without systemic illness favors benign disease
★ **Urinary retention, saddle anesthesia, bilateral weakness** → cauda equina emergency
Fever, weight loss, night pain, trauma, or progressive weakness → targeted urgent evaluation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Paraspinal injury causes localized pain; degenerative narrowing or disk extrusion compresses neural structures

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ No red flags → **no initial imaging**, including routine radiographs
Focused strength, reflex, sensory, gait examination; straight-leg raise supports lower lumbar radiculopathy
★ Suspected infection, malignancy, cord compression → **MRI**; suspected fracture → radiograph or CT
Persistent symptoms despite about 6 weeks' care → MRI if intervention being considered
Suspected spinal infection → ESR/CRP, blood cultures; normal temperature does not exclude infection

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Continue activity**, no heavy lifting until pain resolves, heat, short NSAID course; avoid prolonged bed rest
Physical therapy if pain persists despite NSAIDs; avoid routine opioids and systemic steroids
Progressive motor deficit or cauda equina → urgent surgical decompression
Refractory disabling radicular pain → epidural injection or diskectomy after imaging correlation

rows.label: Complications
items: Chronic pain, functional limitation, medication dependence
Untreated compression → permanent bladder, bowel, sexual, or motor dysfunction

rows.label: Prevention
items: Core strengthening, regular exercise, ergonomic lifting, weight management

rows.label: Mimics
items: AAA: abdominal pulsatile mass, vascular risk, hypotension
Renal colic: flank-to-groin pain, hematuria; inflammatory back pain: improves with exercise
Vascular claudication: calf pain, bicycling too; standing still relieves; weak pulses alone don't exclude stenosis

table.title: Mechanical patterns
rows: Leg pain below knee; cough aggravates
Shopping-cart sign; pulses usually preserved; MRI confirms

low-back-pain.evidence: Not checked online; established generalist back-pain evaluation.

lung-cancer.name: Lung cancer
lung-cancer.scope: Non-small cell, small cell, paraneoplastic syndromes, Pancoast, screening
lung-cancer.core: Persistent cough, hemoptysis, weight loss, or a suspicious lung lesion requires tissue diagnosis and staging before treatment selection.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Smoking, radon, asbestos, occupational carcinogens, prior thoracic radiation; adenocarcinoma also occurs in never-smokers
Leading cause of cancer death in men and women; smoking is the predominant risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Recurrent focal pneumonia, hoarseness, unexplained pleural effusion
★ **Pancoast tumor**: shoulder/ulnar-arm pain + ipsilateral Horner syndrome
SVC obstruction: facial swelling, neck-vein distention; cord compression or airway compromise requires urgent action
Painful long-bone periostitis ± clubbing/joint swelling → **hypertrophic osteoarthropathy**, a lung cancer complication

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Bronchogenic malignant transformation → local invasion, lymphatic spread, hematogenous metastasis
Ectopic hormone production and immune cross-reactivity cause paraneoplastic syndromes
Central endobronchial tumor → bronchial obstruction → **post-obstructive pneumonia**, atelectasis, lobar collapse
Ectopic **ACTH** (polypeptide; cortisol excess secondary) → hyperpigmentation, hypertension, hypokalemic alkalosis, proximal weakness

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Suspicious finding → **contrast chest CT**; biopsy easiest site that establishes highest stage
Central lesion/nodes → bronchoscopy/EBUS; peripheral lesion → CT-guided biopsy; effusion → cytology
PET/CT for extracranial staging, brain MRI for selected stages/small-cell disease; pulmonary function before resection
Molecular profiling and PD-L1 guide advanced NSCLC treatment; suspicious nodes often require pathologic staging

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Early operable NSCLC → **surgical resection + nodal evaluation**; inoperable localized → stereotactic radiation
Locally advanced NSCLC → combined systemic treatment/radiation ± surgery in selected patients
Metastatic NSCLC → biomarker-directed agents or immunotherapy/chemotherapy
★ Small-cell → **platinum + etoposide**, stage-dependent radiation/immunotherapy; surgery rarely used
SVC syndrome from small-cell → urgent **chemotherapy** ± radiation; stent if severe; diuretics not definitive

rows.label: Complications
items: Brain/bone/adrenal/liver metastases, malignant effusion, thrombosis, respiratory failure
Radiation pneumonitis; checkpoint inhibitors → immune pneumonitis/endocrinopathies

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ USPSTF: **annual low-dose CT**, age 50–80, ≥20 pack-years, current smoking or quit <15 years
Stop after 15 quit-years or limited curative candidacy; **ACS omits quit-time restriction**
Smoking cessation and radon mitigation; chest radiographs do not substitute for screening CT

rows.label: Mimics
items: TB/fungal granuloma: microbiologic evidence; PET uptake not specific for cancer
Hamartoma: fat/popcorn calcification; pneumonia: clinical/radiographic response to antibiotics

lung-cancer.evidence: Screening checked 2026-10-30: [USPSTF 2021](https://www.uspreventiveservicestaskforce.org/uspstf/recommendation/lung-cancer-screening), [ACS 2023 guideline](https://acsjournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.3322/caac.21811); treatment: established stage-based framework.

measures-of-disease-frequency.name: Measures of disease frequency
measures-of-disease-frequency.scope: Incidence, prevalence, cumulative incidence, incidence rate, attack rate, case fatality rate, mortality rate
measures-of-disease-frequency.core: Disease frequency requires a numerator, eligible denominator, and time frame; new events, existing disease, and deaths answer different questions.

rows.label: Definition
items: Population at risk excludes people already affected or unable to develop the outcome
Person-time sums observation until disease, death, loss to follow-up, or study end

rows.label: Interpret
items: ★ **Prevalence ≈ incidence × average duration** in steady state; compatible time units
Longer survival increases existing disease burden even without more new diagnoses
Cumulative incidence is probability; incidence density has inverse-time units

rows.label: Use when
items: ★ Variable follow-up/open cohort → **person-time denominator**; fixed cohort/interval → risk
Prevalence → service planning; attack rate → outbreak food/exposure investigation
Primary prevention → fewer new cases → monitor **incidence**, not prevalence

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Case fatality denominator: cases; mortality denominator: population**
Deaths attributed to disease ÷ all deaths = proportionate mortality, not mortality rate
Cross-sectional surveys cannot directly establish incidence or temporal causation

table.title: Independent examples
rows: Current cases ÷ population at one time
New outbreak cases ÷ exposed at-risk people

measures-of-disease-frequency.evidence: Established epidemiologic definitions; no guideline-dependent recommendation.

medical-errors-and-patient-safety.name: Medical errors and patient safety
medical-errors-and-patient-safety.scope: Near miss, adverse event, error disclosure, root cause analysis, structured sign-outs and handoffs
medical-errors-and-patient-safety.core: Protect the patient first, disclose errors honestly, and redesign systems to reduce recurrence.

rows.label: Principle
items: Just culture: distinguish human error, risky shortcuts, and reckless conduct
Psychological safety enables reporting; accountability and system improvement can coexist
Effective communication: bedside verbal handoff with patient → real-time feedback, shared mental model

rows.label: Do
items: ★ **Stabilize and mitigate harm**, notify supervising clinician, preserve relevant clinical information
★ Disclose facts, consequences, **apology**, treatment/prevention plans; update uncertainties
★ Report through institutional safety system; document clinical facts and disclosure in medical record

rows.label: Don't
items: Avoid concealment, altered records, premature blame, or speculation about causation
Do not rely on education alone when workflow permits predictable repeated errors
Do not trust result delivery alone (fax, mail); **test-tracking log** verifies receipt, review, follow-up

rows.label: Exceptions
items: Reckless impairment/dangerous conduct → remove from unsafe duties; institutional escalation

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Root cause analysis**: retrospective system investigation; identify multiple contributors
Failure mode and effects analysis: prospective hazard assessment before harm
Handoff: standardized I-PASS/SBAR, pending tasks, contingency plans, receiver synthesis/read-back

table.title: Event classification
